SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r4.claim: Al-Zumar omits mā because the event is ordinary: when they arrive, the gates are opened.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r4.anchor: وهنا الأمر عادي إذا جاءوا فُتحت الأبواب

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r6.claim: The name al-Zumar, “The Throngs,” comes from the disbelievers being driven to Hell and believers to the Garden in throngs.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r6.anchor: The sūrah takes its title from the mention of the disbelievers being driven to Hell in throngs in v. 71

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.claim: The call to repent in verses 54–67 leads into the final extended contrast between the believers’ and disbelievers’ ends in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.anchor: This is followed by an exhortation to turn to God in repentance

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r1.claim: The just judgment sends deniers and sinners to Hell and the reverent believers who avoid violating God’s commands to Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r1.anchor: münkir ve mücrimlerin cezalandırılmak üzere cehenneme; âyetteki deyimiyle müttakilerin yani Allah’a saygı duyup hükümlerini çiğnemekten sakınmaya özen göstermiş müminlerin de cennete gönderilmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r2.claim: The rebuke by Hell’s keepers indirectly warns people in this life, while they still have an opportunity to change.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r2.anchor: Cehennem bekçilerinin, oraya getirilenlere soracakları soruya dair kınama mahiyetindeki ifadeler, aslında bu dünyada henüz ellerinde fırsat bulunanlar için dolaylı bir uyarı maksadı taşımaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r5.claim: The resurrection, judgment, scales, path, Paradise, and Hell exceed human knowledge because they are unrealized, unique events; they belong to faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r5.anchor: henüz gerçekleşmediği, örneği yaşanmadığı için –tekrarı mümkün olmayan her olay gibi– insanların bilgi sınırlarını aşmakta, iman alanına girmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r6.claim: Qur’anic descriptions make afterlife realities concrete to evoke sound associations and fruitful effects in people’s hearts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r6.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de bunlarla ilgili açıklamalar, tasvirler genellikle insanların zihinlerinde olabildiğince isabetli çağrışımlar ve gönüllerinde verimli etkiler doğmasını sağlayacak şekilde somutlaştırılarak verilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r7.claim: These figurative descriptions cannot be fully and correctly interpreted; individual exegeses are personal understandings, not binding certainties for others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r7.anchor: Bu temsilî açıklamaları tam ve doğru olarak tefsir ve te’vil etmemiz mümkün değildir; bu hususta yapılan yorumlar, te’viller ancak onu yapan kişilerin kendilerine ait yorum ve anlayışlar olup başkalarını bağlayıcı nitelikte kesin bilgiler değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r8.claim: The sound approach is to believe without doubt in the verses and authentic hadith, focus on their purpose, and live accordingly even when their essential meanings remain unclear.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:71/r8.anchor: onların bildirdiklerine şeksiz şüphesiz iman etmek, açıklamaların amacına yönelmek ve bu imanın gereğince yaşamaktır.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r9.claim: The closing verses depict the respective fates of Hell's and Paradise's inhabitants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r9.anchor: details of the circumstances of the dwellers of Hell and Paradise are depicted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p570/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p570/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p570/r4.claim: The final section presents the fates of Paradise's and Hell's inhabitants to wake those who indulge in complacent hopes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p570/r4.anchor: so that the eyes of those who are having sweet dreams are opened.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r1.claim: The disbelievers under discussion are the idolaters; associating partners with God is disbelief, since only pure monotheism is acceptable and shirk contaminates belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r1.anchor: polytheism ( shirk) is disbelief ( kufr). Only that belief in God is considerable to Him which is based on pure monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r2.claim: After the witnesses testify, all guilty of disbelief are led to Hell, whose seven gates receive groups classified by their sins.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r2.anchor: once these testimonies end all those guilty of disbelief will be led to Hell. Once they come near it, its gates will be opened.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r3.claim: Hell's keepers rebuke the doomed by asking whether messengers came to recite God's revelations and warn them of this meeting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r3.anchor: they will rebuke them on seeing their horrible fate and ask them whether messengers of God came to them to inform them of the horrors of this Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r4.claim: The doomed acknowledge messengers came, but their own wretched response caused God's punishment to be imposed on them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r4.anchor: these people will confess their crime and say that messengers did come to them yet it was their wretched response

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r5.claim: The phrase 'decree of punishment' refers to God's comprehensive decision, announced to Satan, that whoever follows Satan will enter Hell with him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r5.anchor: refers to the total decision of God which He pronounced before Satan in response to the latter’s challenge.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r6.claim: Sūrah Mulk gives a fuller confession: the condemned rejected the warner, denied revelation, and regret that they neither listened nor reasoned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p576/r6.anchor: Thus the words of Sūrah Mulk are: اَمَّلُك َيِقْلُأُ اَهیِف جٌْوَف ْمُهَلَأََس اَهُتَنَزَخ ْمَلَأُ ْمُكِتْأََی رٌیِذَن

IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r5.claim: They read both occurrences of فتحت with a doubled tāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ﴿ فتحت ﴾ ﴿ وفتحت ﴾ مشددتين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r6.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائى
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r6.claim: They read both occurrences of فتحت with a light tāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p563/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ فتحت ﴾ ﴿ وفتحت ﴾ يخففون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد والأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd and al-Akhfash define الزمر as separate groups arriving one after another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r7.anchor: الزمر: جمع زمرة، قال أبو عبيد والأخفش: جماعات متفرقة، بعضها إثر بعض.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r8.claim: A poetic line about successive groups illustrates the meaning of الزمر; the poet is unnamed in the source.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p199#3/r8.anchor: قال: حتى احزألت زمر بعد زمر ويقال: تزمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r10.claim: Being driven conveys urging and usually force; the answer to إذا is فتحت أبوابها, indicating Hell's doors stay shut until the condemned arrive, then open and close on them like prison gates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r10.anchor: والسوق يقتضي الحث على المسير بعنف، وهو الغالب فيه. وجواب إذا: فتحت أبوابها، ودل ذلك على أنه لا يفتح إلا إذا جاءت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r11.claim: The doors of Hell are seven, as stated in al-Ḥijr; the light and heavy readings of فتحت were discussed earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r11.anchor: وتقدم ذكر قراءة التخفيف والتشديد في فتحت وأبوابها سبعة، كما ذكر في سورة الحجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r12.claim: The keepers' question is a reprimand; the messengers are described as being from the condemned people themselves, of their kind, so they could understand and approach them easily.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r12.anchor: وقال لهم خزنتها، على سبيل التقريع والتوبيخ، ألم يأتكم رسل منكم: أي من جنسكم، تفهمون ما ينبئونكم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r13.speaker: ابن هرمز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r13.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads تأتكم with feminine ت; most readers use masculine ي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز: تأتكم بتاء التأنيث والجمهور: بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r14.claim: The messengers recited revealed scriptures bringing glad tidings and warning, including warning of the Resurrection Day and its punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r14.anchor: يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم: أي الكتب المنزلة للتبشير والنذارة، وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا: وهو يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r15.claim: The condemned admit that messengers came, recited, and warned them, thereby acknowledging that the proof was established against them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p223/r15.anchor: قالوا بلى: أي قد جاءتنا، وتلوا وأنذروا، وهذا اعتراف بقيام الحجة عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r1.claim: The decreed word of punishment is Gods declaration that He will fill Hell with the unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r1.anchor: لأملأن جهنم . على الكافرين: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r2.claim: Calling them unbelievers explicitly instead of using a pronoun names the quality that merits their punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r2.anchor: على الكافرين: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر، أي علينا، صرحوا بالوصف الموجب لهم العقاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r3.claim: After the exchange with the keepers, the condemned are ordered into Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p224/r3.anchor: ولما فرغت محاورتهم مع الملائكة، أمروا بدخول النار

MAJAZ:v2p191/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p191/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p191/r1.claim: Zumaran means separated groups following one another; its singular is zumrah, and al-Akhṭal uses zumar for a group.
MAJAZ:v2p191/r1.anchor: جماعات فى تفرقة وبعضهم على أثر بعض واحدتها زمرة قال الأخطل

JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r1.speaker: عاصم، وحمزة، والكسائي
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r1.claim: They read futiḥat with a light consonant in both occurrences; the other readers double it.
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: فتحت بالتخفيف في الحرفين، الباقون بالتشديد.

JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r6.claim: The answer to idhā may be “its gates were opened,” with the following w- treated as extra; the implied construction joins the opening to the arrival.
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r6.anchor: قيل: (وفتحت)، وقيل: قوله: (وقال لهم خزنتها) والواو زائدة تقديره

JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r10.claim: One explanation for the w- before Paradise’s gates, absent from the Hell passage, is that Paradise has eight gates while Hell has seven.
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r10.anchor: قيل: لأن أبواب النار سبعة وأبواب الجنة ثمانية، ففرق بينهما للإعلام بهذا المعنى.

JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r11.claim: The Qur’anic expression about Moses and Aaron having the Criterion and light is another example of a conjunction understood as apposition.
JISHUMI:v8p6096#2/r11.anchor: كقوله: (ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء) يعني: ضياء.

JISHUMI:v8p6099/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6099/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6099/r18.claim: The question “Had messengers not come to you?” rebukes Hell’s inhabitants and indicates that their acts originated from themselves.
JISHUMI:v8p6099/r18.anchor: توبيخهم لأهل النار أن الفعل حادث من جهتهم [*].

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r3.claim: A reading has nadhar (we warn) with nūn carrying ḍamma.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r4.claim: The addition of ‘today’ refers to the time of the addressees' entry into Hell, not the Resurrection Day; day and days commonly denote periods of hardship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r4.anchor: أرادوا لقاء وقتكم هذا ، وهو وقت دخولهم النار لا يوم القيامة . وقد جاء استعمال اليوم والأيام مستفيضا في أوقات الشدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r5.claim: They admit that messengers came and recited to them, but God's sentence to fill Hell became binding because of their evil deeds, namely disbelief and error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p149/r5.anchor: { قالوا بلى } أتونا وتلوا علينا ، ولكن وجبت علينا كلمة الله لأملأن جهنم ، لسوء أعمالنا ، كما قالوا : غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين .

TABATABAI:39:71-74/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r1.claim: Hell's wardens are angels who rebuke its entrants by asking whether human messengers had recited their Lord's signs to them; they admit this but confess disbelief and denial.
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r1.anchor: وهم الملائكة الموكلون عليها يقولون لهم تهجينا وإنكارا عليهم { ألم يأتكم رسل منكم }

TABATABAI:39:71-74/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r2.claim: The word of punishment is God's declaration that those who disbelieve and deny the signs will remain in the Fire; the wardens speak the response in context.
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r2.anchor: القائل - على ما يفيده السياق - خزنة جهنم

TABATABAI:39:71-74/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r3.claim: Calling this a wretched abode for the arrogant shows that the condemned are those who rejected God's signs and obstinately resisted truth.
TABATABAI:39:71-74/r3.anchor: وفي قوله { فبئس مثوى المتكبرين } دلالة على أن هؤلاء الذين كفروا هم المكذبون بآيات الله المعاندون للحق

TABATABAI:39:62-75/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r9.claim: One report from Ali says Hell has seven stacked gates or levels, naming them from the lowest Jahannam upward through Lahza, Hutama, Saqar, Jahim, Sa'ir, and Hāwiya.
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r9.anchor: ما روي عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أن جهنم لها سبعة أبواب أطباق بعضها فوق بعض

TABATABAI:39:62-75/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r10.claim: A narration of al-Kalbi reverses the order, with Hāwiya lowest and Jahannam highest.
TABATABAI:39:62-75/r10.anchor: وفي رواية الكلبي أسفلها الهاوية وأعلاها جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r1.claim: After summarizing that every soul is repaid for its deeds in 39:70, Razi explains the punishment scene, then the reward scene, closing the sūra.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r1.anchor: شرح أحوال أهل القيامة على سبيل الإجمال

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r2.speaker: ابن زيدان
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r2.claim: Ibn Zaydān says the unbelievers are driven to Hell violently and by force.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيدان : سوق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم يكون بالعنف والدفع

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r3.speaker: ابن زيدان
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r3.claim: Ibn Zaydān's reading of forced driving is supported by 52:13, 107:2, and 19:86, which use language of pushing or driving.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r3.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا }

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r4.claim: “Zumar” means separate successive companies, one group following another.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r4.anchor: وأما الزمر ، فهي الأفواج المتفرقة بعض في أثر بعض

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r5.claim: The gates of Hell are opened when the unbelievers reach it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r5.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أبواب جهنم إنما تفتح عند وصول أولئك إليها

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r6.claim: The gatekeepers mean messengers from the unbelievers' own human kind.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r6.anchor: يتلون عليكم ءايات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هاذا

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r7.claim: “Meeting this day” means meeting the time of entering Hell, not the Resurrection Day; Arabic commonly uses “day” for a time of hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r7.anchor: أراد لقاء وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولهم النار ، لا يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r8.claim: The unbelievers admit that messengers did come and recite God's signs to them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r8.anchor: فعند هذا تقول الكفار : بلى قد أتونا وتلوا علينا

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r9.claim: Razi reads their response as admitting that the sentence of punishment has applied; one under that sentence cannot escape, so the blessed do not become wretched nor the wretched blessed.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r9.anchor: ومن حقت عليه كلمة العذاب فكيف يمكنه الخلاص من العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r10.claim: The exchange indicates there is no binding obligation before revealed law: the messengers' arrival leaves the punished with no excuse, which would be pointless if revelation were not a condition of liability.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r10.anchor: دلت الآية على أنه لا وجوب قبل مجيء الشرع

RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r11.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r11.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that if entry followed only a fixed decree, the angels' rebuke of the arrogant would be pointless; they say entry is for arrogance toward prophets and rejection of their proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v27p19/r11.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لو كان دخولهم النار لأجل أنه حقت عليهم كلمة العذاب

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r1.claim: Those with heavy scales are separated from those with light scales; the latter are thrust into Hell violently.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r1.anchor: Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will then be separated from those whose scales are light

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r2.claim: The opening of Hell’s gates is compared with 16:29.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r2.anchor: After the gates of Hell are opened (cf. 16:29)

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r3.claim: Hell’s keepers are said to be nineteen angels.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r3.anchor: its keepers, who are said to be nineteen angels (see 74:30c)

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r4.claim: The keepers’ question about messengers is rhetorical rebuke, with parallels in 40:50 and 67:8–9.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r4.anchor: ask the disbelievers this rhetorical question by way of rebuke (cf. 40:50; 67:8–9)

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r5.claim: The disbelievers admit a warner came, but say they denied him and claimed God sent nothing down; they recognize that listening and understanding would have kept them from the Blaze.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r5.anchor: The disbelievers will answer in the affirmative, saying, Indeed, a warner came unto us, but we denied him

STUDYQURAN:39:71/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r6.claim: Their late admission cannot avert punishment because they were warned and given ample opportunity to repent; thus the Word of punishment came due.
STUDYQURAN:39:71/r6.anchor: their now belated affirmation can do nothing to forestall their impending punishment

BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r1.claim: The disbelievers are driven with their leader in successive groups; zumar is a plural of zumra, a small group, and derives from zamr, sound made by a gathering.
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r1.anchor: مع إمامهم حال كونهم {زمرا} : جماعة جماعة

BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r2.claim: The Persian gloss of سوق is driving; they are driven after the reckoning by God's simple command.
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r2.anchor: (راندن) ؛ أي : سيقوا إليها بعد إقامة الحساب بأمر يسير

BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r3.claim: They are driven harshly and in humiliation in separate waves ordered according to degrees of error and wickedness; Hell scowls at them as they scowled at commands and their bearers.
BURSEVI:v8p106#3/r3.anchor: وذلك بالعنف والإهانة حال كونهم أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في إثر بعض

BURSEVI:v8p107/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107/r1.claim: حتى introduces a narrative clause after the preceding sentence, and the answer to إذا is فتحت أبوابها.

BURSEVI:v8p107/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107/r2.claim: They arrive at Hell in humiliation and disgrace.
BURSEVI:v8p107/r2.anchor: (تاجون بيايند بدوزخ بر صفت دلت وخوارى)

BURSEVI:v8p107/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107/r3.claim: Hell has seven gates, as stated in 15:44; leaving them closed until the disbelievers arrive heightens its horror and heat.

BURSEVI:v8p107/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r4.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
BURSEVI:v8p107/r4.claim: As'ilat al-Hikam says the gates are closed like prison doors, forcing the people of Hell to wait for them to open as humiliation and rebuke.
BURSEVI:v8p107/r4.anchor: قال في "أسئلة الحكم" : أهل النار يجدونها مغلقة الأبواب

BURSEVI:v8p107/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107/r5.claim: Bursevi calls the wait at the gates spiritual punishment, worse than bodily pain; prolonged standing in terror can make an unbeliever beg God for relief even by means of the Fire.
BURSEVI:v8p107/r5.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا من قبيل العذاب الروحاني ، وهو أشد من العذاب الجسماني

BURSEVI:v8p107/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107/r6.claim: The seven gates signify seven blameworthy traits—pride, stinginess, greed, lust, envy, anger, and rancor; everyone entering Hell passes through one, so the soul must be purified of them.
BURSEVI:v8p107/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى الأوصاف الذميمة النفسانية السبعة : وهي الكبر والبخل والحرص والشهوة والحسد والغضب والحقد

TAB-FULL:v20p264#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p264#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p264#2/r1.claim: The disbelievers are gathered and driven to the fire prepared for them on Judgment Day in successive groups and parties.

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r1.claim: Hell has seven opened gates; its keepers, the custodians, question the disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r1.anchor: قال الذين كفروا مجيبين لخزنة جهنم

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r2.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers from among the disbelievers recited God's revealed Book and proofs sent to their peoples.

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r3.claim: The messengers warned them about what they would meet that day.

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r4.claim: An alternative explanation takes the warning to mean that they were warned about their destination on that day.
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r4.anchor: أن يكون معناه: وينذرونكم مصيركم إلى هذا اليوم

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r5.claim: The disbelievers admit messengers came from their own people and warned them, but say God's sentence of punishment became due because they disbelieved.
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r5.anchor: قال الذين كفروا مجيبين لخزنة جهنم: بلى قد أتتنا الرسل منا،

TAB-FULL:v20p265/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r6.claim: Qatada says God's sentence of punishment became due because of their deeds.
TAB-FULL:v20p265/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين}

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r1.claim: خزنة means keepers of a store; the word here rebukes and reproaches the people in painful humiliation.

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r2.claim: The keepers are the angels appointed to guard Hell and punish its inhabitants.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r2.anchor: حفظة جهنم وزبانيتها وهم : الملائكة الموكلون بتعذيب أهلها

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r3.claim: The messengers were humans of the addressees’ own kind, making it easier to consult them and understand their speech.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r3.anchor: من جنسكم آدميون مثلكم ليسهل عليكم مراجعتهم وفهم كلامهم

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r4.claim: God’s signs are what He revealed to the prophets.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r4.anchor: وهو ما أنزل الله على الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r5.claim: The messengers warned them by frightening them with the consequences.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r5.anchor:
يخوفونكم.
{لقآء يومكم هاذا} ؛ أي : وقتكم هذا

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r6.claim: This means the time of entering Hell, not the Resurrection Day: ‘day’ is commonly used for a time of distress, and the Resurrection is not exclusive to disbelievers.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r6.anchor: وقت دخولهم النار لا يوم القيامة.

BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r7.claim: Their reproach grounds accountability in messengers’ arrival and delivery of scripture, evidence that there is no obligation before revealed law.
BURSEVI:v8p107#2/r7.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع من حيث أنهم عللوا توبيخهم بإتيان الرسل وتبليغ الكتب

BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r1.claim: They admit the messengers came, recited, and warned them, but their admission comes when confession can no longer benefit them.
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r1.anchor: وأنذرونا فأقروا في وقت لا ينفعهم الإقرار والاعتراف

BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r2.claim: The binding sentence of punishment is God’s declaration to Iblis that He will fill Hell with him and his followers.
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r2.anchor: لاملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p107#3/r3.claim: They explain that they were among Iblis’s followers: they denied the messengers and claimed God had sent nothing.

TABATABAI:39:69-73/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r12.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r12.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines sawq as urging someone onward to travel.
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r12.anchor: السوق بالفتح فالسكون - على ما في المجمع - الحث على السير

TABATABAI:39:69-73/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r13.speaker: الصحاح
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r13.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines zumar as groups of people.
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r13.anchor: والزمر جمع زمرة وهي - كما في الصحاح - الجماعة من الناس

TABATABAI:39:69-73/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r14.claim: The unbelievers are urged toward Hell in successive groups; when they reach it, its seven gates are opened for their entry.
TABATABAI:39:69-73/r14.anchor: والمعنى { وسيق } وحث على السير { الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا } جماعة بعد جماعة

THALABI:v8p256/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p256/r8.claim: The unbelievers are driven violently, dragged on their faces to Hell in successive groups, with each community kept separate.
THALABI:v8p256/r8.anchor: وسيق الذين كفروا سوقا عنيفا يسحبون على وجوههم إلى جهنم زمرا أفواجا بعضها على أثر بعض

THALABI:v8p256/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد والأخفش
THALABI:v8p256/r9.claim: Abu Ubayd and al-Akhfash say zumar means groups gathered separately; zumra is its singular.
THALABI:v8p256/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد والأخفش: يعني جماعات في تفرقة، واحدتها زمرة.

THALABI:v8p256/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p256/r10.claim: Hell has seven gates, and they had been closed before the unbelievers arrived.
THALABI:v8p256/r10.anchor: حتى إذا جاؤها وفتحت أبوابها السبعة وكانت قبل ذلك مغلقة

THALABI:v8p256/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r11.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v8p256/r11.claim: The Kufans lighten the two occurrences of were opened; the other readers double the consonant to indicate repeated or abundant opening.
THALABI:v8p256/r11.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله: (فتحت) و (فتحت) فخففها أهل الكوفة، وشددهما الآخرون على التكثير.

THALABI:v8p256/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p256/r12.claim: Hell's keepers ask the unbelievers by way of rebuke and reproach whether messengers warned them of this day's meeting with God.
THALABI:v8p256/r12.anchor: وقال لهم خزنتها توبيخا وتقريعا لهم ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم

THALABI:v8p256/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p256/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p256/r13.claim: The unbelievers' answer that punishment became binding refers to God's declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and humankind.
THALABI:v8p256/r13.anchor: قالوا بلى ولكن حقت وجبت كلمة العذاب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:71/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:71/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:71/r1.claim: The disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups and successive companies.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:71/r1.anchor: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا } جماعات وأفواجا

QASHANI:39:71-73/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:71-73/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:71-73/r1.claim: The veiled are driven to Hell by their deeds and guided there by the lower self's desire and downward inclination.
QASHANI:39:71-73/r1.anchor: { وسيق } المحجوبون { إلى جهنم } بسائق العمل وقائد الهوى النفسي والميل السفلي

QASHANI:39:71-73/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:71-73/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:71-73/r2.claim: Hell's gates open when they arrive because it eagerly longs for them and is suited to receive them.
QASHANI:39:71-73/r2.anchor: لشدة شوقها إليهم وقبولها لهم لما بينهما من المناسبة

QASHANI:39:71-73/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:71-73/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:71-73/r3.claim: Hell's keepers, Mālik and the zabāniya, symbolize bodily nature and the earthly angelic realm assigned to lower selves.
QASHANI:39:71-73/r3.anchor: { وقال لهم خزنتها } من مالك والزباينة، أي: الطبيعة الجسمانية والملكوت الأرضية الموكلة بالنفوس السفلية

BAQILLANI:v1p9/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r1.claim: The Qur'an's descent through the Trustworthy Spirit to Muhammad in clear Arabic makes him a warner and establishes the Qur'an's language as a proof.
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r1.anchor: فلولا أن كونه بهذا اللسان حجة لم يعقب كلامه الأول به

BAQILLANI:v1p9/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r2.claim: Many sūras opened by disconnected letters are structured from beginning to end to establish the Qur'an's compelling proof and inimitability.
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r2.anchor: وكثير من هذه السور إذا تأملته فهو من أوله إلى آخره مبني على لزوم حجة القرآن

BAQILLANI:v1p9/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r3.claim: In Sūrat al-Muʾmin, disputing God's signs is called disbelief; the account of earlier peoples' rejection and punishment supports this warning.
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r3.anchor: فدل على أن الجدال في تنزيله كفر وإلحاد

BAQILLANI:v1p9/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r4.claim: The angels' prayer for believers shows that accepting the Qur'an's conclusive proof is praiseworthy, just as rejecting it deserves blame.
BAQILLANI:v1p9/r4.anchor: فلولا أنه برهان قاهر لم يذم الكفار على العدول عنه ولم يحمد المؤمنين على المصير إليه

BURHAN:v1p373#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r3.claim: Five occurrences are disputed, but the author says prohibition of stopping is preferable because the continuation links backward and forward.
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: لأن ما بعدها متصل بها وبما قبلها وهى خمسة مواضع

BURHAN:v2p183/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p183/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p183/r5.claim: In حتى إذا جاؤوها وفتحت أبوابها, حتى requires completion; the implied wording repeats جاؤوها before the doors are opened.
BURHAN:v2p183/r5.anchor: لا بد لها من تمام وتأويله حتى إذا جاءوها جاءوها

BURHAN:v3p187/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p187/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p187/r11.claim: In the Fire passage, the doors open when its people arrive; the version without waw makes arrival the condition for opening.
BURHAN:v3p187/r11.anchor: وكقوله تعالى ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها وفتحت أبوابها ﴾ 5 أي حتى إذا جاءوها وقد فتحت أبوابها

BURHAN:v3p187/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p187/r13.speaker: أبو علي
BURHAN:v3p187/r13.claim: Abu Ali rejects the waw-of-eight account: Hell’s doors were closed, so arrival triggers opening; Paradise’s waw is circumstantial, meaning they arrive with its doors already open.
BURHAN:v3p187/r13.anchor: فقال أبو علي لا أقول كما قال إنما تركت الواو في النار لأنها مغلقة

BURHAN:v1p342/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p342/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p342/r1.claim: Stopping and resuming is a major discipline: it guides recitation, interpretation, inference, and avoidance of problematic readings; al-Zajjaj, Ibn al-Anbari, Ibn Abbad, al-Dani, and al-Umani wrote on it.
BURHAN:v1p342/r1.anchor: وهو فن جليل وبه يعرف كيف أداء القرآن ويترتب على ذلك فوائد كثيرة

SULAMI:v2p204#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p204#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p204#5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ describes three ranks of Paradise greeting: the lowest are greeted by its keepers, the middle by angels entering through every gate, and the highest by God Himself.
SULAMI:v2p204#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : السلام في الجنة من وجوه منهم من تسلم عليه خزنة الجنة يقولون ﴿ سلام عليكم طبتم ﴾ وهؤلاء ادناهم

ITQAN:v2p343/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r7.claim: Ḥaqqat means it has become due or already come to pass.

ITQAN:v1p235/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p235/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p235/r7.claim: Five “balā” instances are disputed, with not pausing preferred; examples occur in al-Baqara, al-Zumar, al-Zukhruf, al-Hadid, and al-Mulk.
ITQAN:v1p235/r7.anchor: الثاني ما فيه خلاف والاختيار المنع وذلك خمسة مواضع في البقرة

NAHHAS:v4p21/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p21/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p21/r15.claim: The Hell account states the answer to إذا; Paradise has waw but an omitted answer. The Kufans call waw extra, which Basrans reject as meaningful coordination.
NAHHAS:v4p21/r15.anchor: وفي قصة أهل الجنة و ( وفتحت ) بالواو فالكوفيون يقولون الواو زائدة

NAHHAS:v4p21/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p21/r17.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
NAHHAS:v4p21/r17.claim: One scholar says Hell's gates were closed until arrival, while Paradise's gates were already open.
NAHHAS:v4p21/r17.anchor: فأما الحكمة في إثبات الواو في الثاني وحذفها من الأول فقد تكلم فيه بعض أهل العلم

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r1.claim: They take zumar as a circumstantial plural of zumra: groups gathering separately, one after another; a cited line says زمر بعد زمر.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r1.anchor: حتى احزألت زمر بعد زمر هذا قول أبي عبيدة والأخفش.

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r2.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says a zumra is a small group, relating the word to a sheep with little hair and a man of little manliness; he also connects it with the ostrich's cry and the derived terms for music and a wanton woman.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب: " الزمرة الجماعة القليلة، ومنه شاة زمرة أي: قليلة الشعر،

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r3.claim: Readers differ over geminating or lightening the ت in فتحت; the author refers to the discussion in Sūrat al-Anʿām without restating the assignments.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r3.anchor: وتقدم خلاف القراء في التشديد والتخفيف في سورة الأنعام.

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r4.speaker: ابن هرمز
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r4.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads ألم تأتكم with a feminine plural ت.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز " ألم تأتكم " بتاء التأنيث الجمع.

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r5.claim: منكم can modify رسل as an adjective or attach to the coming expressed by أتى.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r5.anchor: و " منكم " صفة ل " رسل " أو متعلق بالإتيان،

SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r6.claim: يتلون is a second adjective qualifying رسل.
SAMIN-DURR:39:71/r6.anchor: و " يتلون " صفة أخرى، و " خالدين " في الموضعين حال مقدرة.

ASAD-NOTES:39:71#n73/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:71#n73/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:71#n73/r1.claim: The sentence of suffering fell due as the ineluctable consequence of the deniers' unrepented sinning.
ASAD-NOTES:39:71#n73/r1.anchor: as an ineluctable consequence of their unrepented sinning.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p723/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p723/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p723/r1.claim: Everyone is driven, but the destination is the point: unbelievers go to Hell and the God-fearing to Paradise; the Qur'an likewise says each soul has a driver and witness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p723/r1.anchor: إذن كلهم يساقون لكن المهم جهة السوق فهؤلاء يُساق بهم إلى الجنة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r2.claim: Hell's gates are normally shut and opening them at arrival startles and terrifies; Paradise's gates are always open, unlike a prison's.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r2.anchor: والفارق أن جهنم هي كالسجن أبوابها مقفلة لا تفتح إلا لداخل أو خارج

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r4.claim: The Hell conditional has an explicit answer; the Paradise conditional has none because human language cannot encompass its blessings, whose answer lies within Paradise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p653/r4.anchor: أما في حال الجنة فلا يوجد جواب للشرط لأنه يضيق ذكر النعمة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p311/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p311/r1.claim: Shadda marks repeated opening of each door; the light form marks one opening and is preferable because the action is not repeated. The doubled form is supported by other door descriptions.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p311/r1.anchor: يقرآن بالتشديد والتخفيف فالحجة لمن شدد أنه أراد تكرير الفعل لأن كل باب منها فتح ودليله إجماعهم على التشديد

NASHR:v2p130/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p130/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p130/r1.claim: Across the listed words that vary between singular and plural, singular readers pause according to their usual hāʾ or tāʾ practice, while plural readings stop with tāʾ.
NASHR:v2p130/r1.anchor: والقسم الذي قرئ بالإفراد وبالجمع ثمانية أحرف

NASHR:v2p130/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p130/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p130/r2.claim: The codices generally write these forms with tāʾ; al-Dani notes an Iraqi-copy exception for the second Yunus occurrence, and the Ghafir spelling may signal either singular or plural, though its tāʾ copies are read plural as far as known.
NASHR:v2p130/r2.anchor: وقد أجمعت المصاحف على كتابة ذلك كله بالتاء إلا ما ذكره الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني

QIRAAT-ER:39:71:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:2#1/r1.claim: Vowel harmony changes the passive vocalic texture but leaves the consonantal verb and procession meaning unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:2#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel-harmony variant colors the passive vocalic texture while preserving the same consonantal verb

QIRAAT-ER:39:71:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:11#1/r1.claim: The doubled reading intensifies the opening, suggesting repeated or multiple gate access, or an emphatically activated opening.
QIRAAT-ER:39:71:11#1/r1.anchor: Canonical doubled reading intensifies the opening, suggesting repeated, multiple, or emphatically activated gate access

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r1.claim: The scene details how the disbelievers are fully requited and how that requital occurs.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r2.claim: Driving them implies forceful, urgent movement; here it conveys humiliation as they are driven in successive groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r2.anchor: والسوق يقتضي الحث على المسير بعنف وإزعاج وهو الغالب ويشعر بالإهانة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines zumrah as a small group and relates the word to sparse hair or scant manliness.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : هي الجماعة القليلة ومنه شاة زمرة قليلة الشعر ورجل زمر قليل المروءة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r4.claim: Another derivation connects zumrah to sound, since a group is rarely without it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم اشتقاق الزمرة من الزمر وهو الصوت

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r5.claim: The groups follow one another, ordered according to their degrees of error and wickedness.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r5.anchor: أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في أثر بعض مترتبة حسب ترتب طبقاتهم في الضلالة والشرارة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r6.claim: Hell’s gates had remained shut until the condemned arrived, like prison doors, and close after they enter.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r6.anchor: وكانت قبل مجيئهم غير مفتوحة فهي كسائر أبواب السجون لا تزال مغلقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r7.claim: More than one reader recites the verb with doubled tāʾ.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r8.claim: The keepers’ question is a reproach and rebuke.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r9.claim: The messengers were of the condemned people’s kind, so they could understand the message and readily consult them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r9.anchor: أي من جنسكم تفهمون ما ينبؤنكم به ويسهل عليكم مراجعتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r10.speaker: ابن هرمز
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r10.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads the verb with feminine tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز ( تأتكم ) بتاء التأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r11.claim: A variant reading has nudhur in place of rusul.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r12.claim: The verses recited to them were revealed for their benefit.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r13.claim: The day is most clearly the time of entering the Fire, since the actual warning concerns punishment and its time; it may instead mean Resurrection, which includes this time or their particular punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r13.anchor: أي وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولكم النار لأن المنذر به الحقيقة العذاب ووقته

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r14.claim: The verse is cited against moral obligation before revealed law: the condemned are rebuked for disbelief after messengers conveyed law and warned them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r14.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع وبخوهم بكفرهم بعد تبليغ الرسل للشرائع وإنذارهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r15.claim: The argument is inferential and assumes disputed generality; rational-duty proponents can say post-message disbelief merits sharper rebuke, while the verbs rule out interpreting the messengers as intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p31#3/r15.anchor: هو دليل إقناعي لأنه إنما يتم على اعتبار المفهوم وعموم الذين كفروا وكلاهما محل نزاع

ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r1.claim: The word of punishment is God’s decree that they are wretched and among the people of the Fire for their bad choice, or His statement to Iblis about filling Hell with him and his followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r1.anchor: والمراد بها الحكم عليهم بالشقاوة وأنهم من أهل النار لسوء اختيارهم أو قوله تعالى لإبليس

ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r2.claim: Calling them disbelievers instead of using a pronoun hints that disbelief is the cause of the punishment; their reply is admission, not an excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p32/r2.anchor: ووضعوا الكافرين موضع ضميرهم للإيماء إلى علية الكفر والكلام اعتراف لا اعتذار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r3.claim: The disbelievers are driven forcefully toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r3.anchor: {وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم} سوقا عنيفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r4.claim: They go in successive groups, each community apart from the others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r4.anchor: {زمرا} أفواجا بعضها على إثر بعض، كل أمة على حدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash gloss zumaran as separate companies; its singular is zumra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والأخفش: "زمرا" أي: جماعات في تفرقة، واحدتها زمرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r6.claim: Hell has seven gates, which had been closed before the disbelievers arrived.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r6.anchor: {حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها} السبعة وكانت مغلقة قبل ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r7.speaker: أهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r7.claim: The Kūfan readers recite the verb without doubling its middle consonant; the other readers double it to convey repeated opening.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r7.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة "فتحت، وفتحت" بالتخفيف، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد على التكثير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r8.claim: The keepers address them in rebuke and reproach.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r9.claim: The messengers were from among the disbelievers' own people.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r10.claim: Ḥaqqat means that the word of punishment became binding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r10.anchor: قالوا بلى ولكن حقت} وجبت، {كلمة العذاب على الكافرين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r11.claim: The word of punishment is God's declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p132#2/r11.anchor: وهو قوله عز وجل: "لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين"

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r2.claim: The disbelievers are driven in successive, separate groups, differing in the degrees of their misguidance and wickedness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r2.anchor: أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في أثر بعض على تفاوت أقدامهم في الضلالة والشرارة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r3.claim: Zumrah may derive from zamr, sound, since a group makes noise; alternatively it denotes a small group, by comparison with words for sparse wool or scant manliness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r3.anchor: واشتقاقها من الزمر وهو الصوت إذ الجماعة لا تخلو عنه، أو من قولهم شاة زمرة قليلة الشعر ورجل زمر قليل المروءة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r4.claim: The gates are opened for the groups to enter; hatta introduces and depicts the sentence that follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r4.anchor: و { حتى } وهي التي تحكي بعدها الجملة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r5.speaker: الكوفون
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r5.claim: The Kufans read فتحت with a light ta.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r6.claim: The guardians address them to rebuke and reproach them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r7.claim: The messengers were from your own kind.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r8.claim: The messengers recited God's signs and warned of the encounter on this day, meaning the time when the condemned enter Hell.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r8.anchor: وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولهم النار

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r9.claim: Their reproach links culpability to the arrival of messengers and delivery of scripture, evidence that there is no obligation before revealed law.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r9.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا تكليف قبل الشرع من حيث إنهم عللوا توبيخهم بإتيان الرسل وتبليغ الكتب

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r10.claim: They concede the messengers came, but God's judgment of wretchedness and Hell has become binding on them; the disbelievers replaces a pronoun to specify who is condemned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r10.anchor: كلمة الله بالعذاب علينا وهو الحكم عليهم بالشقاوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r11.claim: An alternative identifies the word of punishment with God's declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:70-73/r11.anchor: وقيل هو قوله لأملان جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r7.claim: Because warning predominates in this setting, the account of recompense begins with the people subject to divine wrath.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r7.anchor: ولما كان الأغلب على هذه المقامات التحذير , قدم في هذه التوفية حال أهل الغضب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r8.claim: After judgment, the disbelievers are driven swiftly by God's command toward Hell because they veiled their intellect and became confused and astray.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r8.anchor: بأمر يسير من قبلنا بعد إقامة الحساب سوقا عنيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r9.claim: Disbelievers are described as those who cover the lights of their intellect, leaving matters confused and themselves astray.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p476/r9.anchor: غطوا أنوار عقولهم , فالتبست عليهم الأمور فضلوا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayd glosses the groups as classified kinds, each person gathered with those whose way resembles his.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r1.anchor: قاله أبو عبيد - أصنافا مصنفين , كل شخص مع من يلائمه في الطريقة الزمرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r2.claim: The word is connected to zamr, a confused sound such as the familiar flute, associated with the sound of a crowd.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r2.anchor: مأخوذة من الزمر وهو صوت فيه التباس كالزمر المعروف لأن ذلك الصوت من لازم الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r3.claim: A gate shut against its intended entrant signals the disbelievers' humiliation; the gates are opened emphatically once all have arrived, as for assembled criminals in prison.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r3.anchor: إغلاق الباب المقصود عن قاصده دالا على صغاره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r4.claim: The gates are flung open rapidly after the criminals assemble, releasing Hell's heat and flames to meet them in a state worse than what they chose in worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r4.anchor: ليخرج إليهم ما كان محبوسا بإغلاقها من الحرارة التي يلقاهم ذكاؤها وشرارها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r5.claim: The keepers' question is a scolding rebuke and reproach that compounds the punishment.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r6.claim: Messengers from among their own people establish the proof more strongly and make it easier for them to consult the messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r6.anchor: ولما كان قيام الحجة بالمجانس أقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r7.claim: Reciting means continually reminding them; this fits the sura's concern with worship and souls' need for reminders because of their deficiencies.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r8.claim: Calling God their Lord softens the admonition and makes acceptance more likely, while also recalling the good news available if they had followed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r8.anchor: ولما كان أمر المحسن أخف على النفس فيكون أدعى إلى القبول

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r9.claim: Warning is more forceful in restraining them, and pointing to this day makes the threatened encounter concrete.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r9.anchor: ولما كان الإنذار أبلغ في الزجر قالوا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r10.claim: The ellipsis (iḥtibāk) links the mention of the Lord first to omitted majesty second, and the later warning to omitted glad tidings first.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r10.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الرب أولا دلالة على حذف الجبروت ثانيا والإنذار ثانيا دليلا على البشارة أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r11.claim: They acknowledge that the messengers came, recited the signs, and warned them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r11.anchor: أي قد أتونا وتلوا علينا وحذرونا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r12.claim: They say punishment became due by a decree established in eternity; specifying disbelievers identifies their defining trait as the cause of entry.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p477/r12.anchor: أي وجبت وجوبا يطابقه الواقع , لا يقدر معه على الانفكاك عنه

DURR-FULL:v7p262/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Hell lashes its people with a neck that strips flesh from their bones down to the ankles.
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن جهنم إذا سيق إليها أهلها تلفحهم بعنق

DURR-FULL:v7p262/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r3.claim: Qatada says the decree of punishment became binding on disbelievers because of their evil deeds.
DURR-FULL:v7p262/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين} قال: بأعمالهم أعمال السوء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r4.claim: This carries out the judgment and full recompense announced in 39:69–70: wrongdoers enter punishment and the righteous enter the abode of reward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r5.claim: The account begins with those due punishment because it renews warning for people unmoved by repeated Qur'anic admonitions; the saved have already responded, so their mention is repeated good news and praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r5.anchor: وابتدىء في الخبر بذكر مستحقي العقاب لأنه الأهم في هذا المقام إذ هو مقام إعادة الموعظة والترهيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r6.claim: Driving means making one walk while another goes ahead and stays beside him; unlike leading, it conveys coercion and humiliation, as in the description of people driven toward death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r6.anchor: والسوق : أن يجعل الماشي ماشيا آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r7.claim: A zumrah is a group followed by another group; the term implies succession rather than an isolated passing group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r7.anchor: والزمر : جمع زمرة ، وهي الفوج من الناس المتبوع بفوج آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r8.claim: Groups reflect different degrees of disbelief: if the threat targets Quraysh, their severity, attitude toward Muslims, and treatment of the Prophet distinguish them; if all polytheists, their kinds of shirk distinguish them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r8.anchor: وإن كان المراد بهم جميع أهل الشرك كما تقتضيه حكاية الموقف مع قوله : { ألم يأتكم رسل } كان تعدد زمرهم على حسب أنواع إشراكهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r9.claim: حتى begins a new sentence, while إذا is a future time adverb usually carrying a conditional sense; the forceful driving continues until arrival at Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p68/r9.anchor: و { حتى } ابتدائية و { إذا } ظرف لزمان المستقبل يضمن معنى الشرط غالبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r1.claim: The majority pronounce the initial letters of sīqa and jīʾa with kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وسيق وجيء بكسر أوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن وثاب وعاصم والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Waththab, Asim, and al-Aʿmash use imāla toward ḍamma in these and similar forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r2.anchor: وقرأها ونظائرها بإشمام الضم: الحسن وابن وثاب وعاصم والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r3.claim: Zumaran means separate groups; its singular is zumra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r3.anchor: زمرا معناه: جماعات متفرقة، واحدها زمرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r4.claim: The opening is the answer to idhā, so the wording places the opening after their arrival; the delay humiliates them, unlike the already-open gates of Paradise in 39:73.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: فتحت جواب إذا، والكلام هنا يقضي أن فتحها إنما يكون بعد مجيئهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r5.claim: The conjunction in the account of Paradise indicates that its gates are found open, like the homes of people arriving for joy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r5.anchor: بخلاف قوله: في أهل الجنة: وفتحت [الزمر: 73] بالواو مؤذنة بأنهم يجدونها مفتوحة كمنازل الأفراح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r6.claim: The majority geminate the tāʾ in both occurrences of fataḥat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «فتحت» بشد التاء في الموضعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وطلحة والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r7.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, Talha, and al-Aʿmash read both forms with a light tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي بتخفيفها، وهي قراءة طلحة والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور والأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r8.claim: The majority read yatikum with yāʾ; al-Aʿraj reads it with tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «يأتكم» بالياء من تحت. وقرأ الأعرج: «تأتكم» بتاء من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r9.claim: The messengers’ being from the people addressed strengthens the proof: their speech and intent should have been easy for them to understand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r9.anchor: وقوله: منكم أعظم في الحجة، أي رسل من جنسكم لا يصعب عليكم مراميهم ولا فهم أقوالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r10.claim: Balā answers a negative question by affirming that messengers did come; naʿam would instead affirm that none came.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r10.anchor: وقولهم: بلى جواب على التقرير على نفي أمر، ولا يجوز هنا الجواب بنعم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r11.claim: The word of punishment is God’s prior decree that they remain eternally in the Fire, as in the divine declaration to Iblis in 38:85.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p542#2/r11.anchor: أي الكلمة المقتضية من الله تعالى تخليدهم في النار، وهي عبارة عن قضائه السابق لهم بذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says zumar are groups arriving separately, one after another; zumra is the singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الزمر جماعات في تفرقة بعضهم على إثر بعض واحدها زمرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r2.claim: “Messengers from among you” means messengers from your own people.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r3.claim: The “word of punishment” is God's declaration, “I will surely fill Hell,” at 7:18.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r3.anchor: أي من أنفسكم و ﴿ كلمة العذاب ﴾ هي قوله ﴿ لأملأن جهنم ﴾ الأعراف 18

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read the verb with gemination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر فتحت وفتحت مشددتين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r5.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p199/r5.claim: ʿAsim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the verb without gemination.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r1.claim: The wretched disbelievers are driven violently toward Hell with rebuke and threats, thirsty as they go; the author links this to the contrast with the gathered righteous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r1.anchor: وإنما يساقون سوقا عنيفا بزجر وتهديد ووعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r2.claim: They are deaf, dumb, and blind, and some walk on their faces, as described in another verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r2.anchor: وهم في تلك الحال صم وبكم وعمي، منهم من يمشي على وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r3.claim: Hell's gates open immediately upon the disbelievers' arrival so their punishment can begin without delay.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r3.anchor: بمجرد وصولهم إليها فتحت لهم أبوابها سريعا، لتعجل لهم العقوبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r4.claim: The keepers are Zabāniyah, harsh in character and powerful, and their questioning rebukes and humiliates the arrivals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r4.anchor: من الزبانية -الذين هم غلاظ الأخلاق، شداد القوى على وجه التقريع والتوبيخ والتنكيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r5.claim: The messengers were of the disbelievers' own kind, so they could speak with and learn from them; their recitation established proofs, and they warned them of this Day's meeting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r5.anchor: أي: من جنسكم تتمكنون من مخاطبتهم والأخذ عنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p118#2/r6.claim: They admit the messengers came, but say punishment became due because they denied and opposed them, turning from truth to falsehood in the misery they deserved.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r1.anchor: فيه أربعة أوجه : أحدها : أفواجا , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r2.anchor: قاله الحسن . الثاني : أمما , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r3.anchor: قاله الكلبي . الثالث : جماعات , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r4.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says they are dispersed groups arriving one after another, with zumra as the singular.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش جماعات متفرقة , بعضها إثر بعض واحدها زمرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r5.speaker: خفاف بن ندبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r5.claim: Khuffaf ibn Nudba's verse illustrates the term for groups arriving in the morning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r5.anchor: قال خفاف بن ندبة : كأن إخراجها في الصبح غادية … من كل شائبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r6.claim: The word may describe being pushed and rebuked with a sound like a pipe, as in the phrase about David's pipes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p137/r6.anchor: الرابع : دفعا وزجرا بصوت كصوت المزمار , ومن قولهم مزامير داود .

MUQATIL:39:71-72/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r1.claim: Those who disbelieved in God's oneness are driven to Hell in groups, with each nation's unbelievers gathered separately.
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r1.anchor: بتوحيد الله { إلى جهنم زمرا } يعنى أفواجا من كفار كل أمة على حدة

MUQATIL:39:71-72/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r2.claim: Hell's gates, previously closed, are opened, and the records that had been folded are spread out.
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r2.anchor: { فتحت أبوابها } يومئذ وكانت مغلقة ونشرت الصحف وكانت مطوية

MUQATIL:39:71-72/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r3.claim: Hell's keepers say messengers from among the people recited God's Quranic signs and warned them of the Resurrection Day.
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r3.anchor: { وقال لهم خزنتها } يعنى خزنة جهنم { ألم يأتكم رسل منكم } يعنى أنفسكم { يتلون عليكم } يعنى يقرءون عليكم { آيات ربكم } القرآن

MUQATIL:39:71-72/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:71-72/r4.claim: The decree of punishment is the word God spoke to Satan that He would fill Hell with him and all who follow him.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r1.claim: The disbelievers are driven violently, like prisoners or rebels taken to imprisonment or execution.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم ﴾ سوقا عنيفا كما يفعل بالاسارى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r2.claim: Zumar is a circumstantial accusative meaning separate groups following one another.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ زمرا ﴾ حال أي افواجا متفرقة بعضها في اثر بعض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r3.speaker: كوفى
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r3.claim: Kufan reciters use the lighter form of the opening verb in both passages about Hell's gates.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها فتحت ﴾ بالتخفيف فيهماكوفى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r5.claim: Hell's keepers are angels assigned to punish its inhabitants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r5.anchor: أي حفظة جهنم وهم الملائكة الموكلون بتعذيب اهلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r6.claim: The messengers were from among humanity, the children of Adam.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ ألم يأتكم رسل منكم ﴾ من بني ادم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r7.claim: Meeting your day means the time of entering Hell, not the Day of Resurrection itself.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r7.anchor: ﴿ يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا ﴾ أي وقتكم هذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r8.claim: They affirm that messengers came and recited God's verses to them.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r9.claim: God's sentence to fill Hell took effect because of their evil deeds; they recall disbelief and error as the cause.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p63#4/r9.anchor: وجبت علينا كلمة الله لاملأن جهنم بسوء اعمالنا كما قالوا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r1.claim: This describes each soul receiving its due: unbelievers are driven to the Fire and believers to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r1.anchor: هذا بيان توفية كل نفس عملها، فيساق الكافر إلى النار والمؤمن إلى الجنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r2.claim: Zumar means groups; its singular zumrah has the same pattern relation as ẓulmah to ghurfah in the cited forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r2.anchor: والزمر: الجماعات واحدتها زمرة كظلمة وغرفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r3.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubayda explain zumar as separate groups following one after another.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش وأبو عبيدة: { زمرا } جماعات متفرقة بعضها إثر بعض.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r4.claim: An unnamed poet’s line describes people visiting a man’s dwelling in groups, one group after another.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وترى الناس إلى منزله
زمرا تنتابه بعد زمر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r5.claim: A second unnamed poet also says that groups follow one another in succession.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r5.anchor:
وقال آخر:
حتى احزألت
زمر بعد زمر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r6.claim: Another gloss takes the word to mean that they are pushed and driven with a sound like a mizmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r6.anchor: وقيل: دفعا وزجرا بصوت كصوت المزمار.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r7.claim: The response to when they arrive is that the gates open, and there are seven gates, as discussed in Surat al-Hijr.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r8.claim: The keepers’ singular is khāzin, just as sadanah is the plural of sādin; they speak in reproach and reprimand.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r8.anchor: واحدهم خازن نحو سدنة وسادن، يقولون لهم تقريعا وتوبيخا.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r9.claim: The Lord’s signs recited by the messengers are the scriptures revealed to the prophets.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r10.claim: To warn them means to frighten them about the Day of Judgment.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r11.claim: Their yes is an admission that messengers came and that the proof had been established against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r11.anchor: أي قد جاءتنا، وهذا اعتراف منهم بقيام الحجة عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r12.claim: The binding word of punishment is God’s declaration that He will fill Hell with jinn and people together.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:71-72/r12.anchor:
وهي قوله تعالى:
لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين
[هود: 119]
